studies.title: Data Center MEP Coordination Failure
studies.problem: Electrical rough-in conflicted with HVAC chase locations; uncoordinated rework was required after both systems were partially installed.
studies.cost: $200K+ in rework, plus a 3-week schedule delay
whatWentWrong: Pre-construction coordination was limited; conflicts weren't identified early
No site walk-through with trades happened before rough-in began
Field Engineer inspections were reactive, not proactive
Escalation happened after the conflict was already built, not before
whatShouldHappenInstead: Pre-construction: walk the drawings with all affected trades and mark conflicts before anyone mobilizes
Before rough-in: hold an on-site coordination meeting and physically mark locations
During rough-in: FE verifies actual placement against the coordinated plan daily
Escalation: any deviation gets a photo and Super notification the same day it's found
tacitKnowledge: Coordination happens on-site, not just at meetings
Prevention is dramatically cheaper than correction
Be the translator between trades — they don't talk to each other unless you make them
Daily walk-throughs catch problems before they turn into rework

yourFramework.step1: Become the central translator between trades
yourFramework.step2: Proactive coordination is roughly 80% of the FE job
yourFramework.step3: Document conflicts early — solutions are cheaper the earlier they're caught
